messages:
jordan: quick sync — I pushed a small kernel change that fuses attention matmul + softmax for the paged-attn path. Can someone run a short microbench on a few seq lengths? patch: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/+/refs/heads/attn-fuse-canary

I want baseline vs canary delta on: 256, 512, 1024, and a long tail 2048. Also check memory peak and 99th token latency. If you see >5% regression at 512/1024, call it out.

samir: tagging in — will run profiling tomorrow morning (PST). Can you confirm dataset and model? also do you want FlashAttention path enabled?

jordan: model is redwood-coder-7b, standard eval shard 12 (same as perf harness). Yes keep FlashAttention on; this change is only for the paged-attn kernel. I suspect a slight win at 512, maybe neutral at 2048.

samir: ok running on H100; I'll run the microbench script:
```bash
./bench/run_microbench.sh --model redwood-coder-7b \
  --seqs 256,512,1024,2048 --batch 1 --iters 200 \
  --pinned-checkpoint refs/heads/attn-fuse-canary
```

I'll capture nvprof / Nsight and KV cache traces. If build-bot finishes CI, I'll use that binary.

build-bot: CI: attn-fuse-canary build started (job #9843)
build-bot: CI: attn-fuse-canary build passed — artifact: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/9843/attn-fuse-canary.tar.gz :thumbsup:

mei: quick question — does the patch change the quantized codepath? we have a quant convo earlier; need to ensure int8 path falls back to safe matmul. show config snippet?

jordan: good call — it only touches float kernels. quantized path should remain unchanged. config we used:
```json
{"runtime": {"enable_paged_attn_fusion": true, "force_flash": false, "quant_fallback": true}}
```

mei: thanks. can we add a guard so quantized kernels explicitly opt-out? otherwise some infra builds might flip flags unexpectedly.

jordan: will add guard in the next commit.

lina: note: please run on both A100 and H100 if possible — we've seen memory allocation differences with paged strategies. On A100 the paged allocator sometimes increases peak by ~200MB.

devops: I can reserve an A100 node for a 2-hour window at 03:00 UTC. @samir confirm if that works. Also suggest disabling preemption on that node for the run.

samir: 03:00 UTC works. reserving H100 and A100 targets. I'll also snapshot the system metrics and collect flamegraphs.

jordan: for the regression check — if 99th token latency regresses >7% on any seq, we'll gate the rollout and revert. If memory peak >10% on A100, we pause. Otherwise we can promote to canary on 10% of traffic.

samir: quick local note — I'll run both the harness (which measures end-to-end serving latency) and a kernel-only bench via the microbench binary to separate infra noise. kernel command: 
```bash
./build/bin/kern_bench --kernel paged_fused_attn --seq 1024 --iters 1000 --warmup 100
```

build-bot: perf-job: started profiling job #9844 (samir)

samir: initial numbers (H100, batch1) — kernel-only: 1024 seq: 28.3ms -> canary 26.7ms (~5.7% win). E2E harness (including I/O): 1024 seq: 33.9ms -> canary 33.1ms (~2.3% win). memory peak: +1.2% on H100. attaching full logs: https://logs.redwood.ai/9844

mei: nice! can you also dump a few instruction counters or perf counters? curious about L2 utilization.

samir: will add perf counters in the next pass. Looks clean so far, no obvious 99th token regressions.

jordan: awesome. @devops when can we promote to canary 10%?

devops: give me 2 hours after you all finish the A100 run and we validate CI artifact. I can stage traffic split in rollout service.

lina: reminder to open a short PR description for the ops team summarizing memory delta and fallback flag. helps ops react quickly if customers hit regressions.

jordan: will do — I'll create PR + short changelog and add the guard for quant path. Thanks everyone, great async sync. :beers:

samir: filing a short follow-up with perf artifacts and flamegraphs now.

build-bot: perf-job: completed (job #9844)
